newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Rubber prices rise sharply at Colombo auction.
newsitem.headline: Rubber prices rise sharply at Colombo auction.

text.p: Rubber prices rose sharply at this week's Colombo auction owing to short supply caused by New Year holidays and drought, brokers said on Friday.
"Very little rubber is coming to Colombo," said a broker at Forbes and Walker. "If the drought continues intakes will be very poor because factories will have no water to make rubber.
"Monsoon rains are expected in May which could interrupt tapping," he added. "There could be short supply till July."
Tapping and production was interrupted because many people stayed away from work in the run up to and after the April 13-14 traditional New Year celebrations.
Best latex one-x, the purest grade, rose to 79.40 rupees per kg ($1.36) on Thursday from 78 rupees last week, according to auction prices made available on Friday, because of the New Year holidays.
Latex crepe number one rose to 79 rupees per kg from 77.50 rupees last week while RSS 1 was unquoted after going for 61 rupees last week.
Tropical Sri Lanka is experiencing a drought after the November-March northeast monsoon failed for a second year in a row. --Colombo newsroom (941) 434319 ($1=Rs.58.48)
